# Switch NX2 - read when the Lichii GUI starts.
# One NAME=VALUE per line. Lines starting with # are ignored.
# A variable already set in the environment wins over this file.
# Between files, the user copy (%APPDATA%\eden\nx2_switches.txt, or
# $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/eden/nx2_switches.txt) wins over this one, so editing this file is never
# needed: copy the lines you want into your own and restart.
#
# Restart the emulator after editing.

# --- Performance tuning defaults for Switch 2 ---
# Offload GPU method/macro execution to the back thread (SPLIT=2 delivers up to +54% FPS alone).
EDEN_NX2_SPLIT=2

# Batch GPU fence syncpoints to reduce host driver overhead and smooth frametimes.
EDEN_NX2_FENCE_BATCH=1

# Leave buffer downloads disabled on Switch 2 (default): forcing downloads (=1) copies back
# 90-220 MB/s of buffers CPU never touches, causing heavy mutex contention and dropping FPS by ~38-63%.
#EDEN_NX2_BUFFER_DOWNLOADS=1

# Paces frame submission 2 frames ahead. Reduces frametime spikes, but adds ~1-2 frames of input latency.
# Enable only if frame pacing stability is preferred over responsive controls.
#EDEN_NX2_FRAMES_AHEAD=2

# --- Experiments: CPUs with several L3 domains (Ryzen 3000/5000 with 8+ cores) ---
# Keep GPU, GPUBack and VulkanWorker on one L3 domain (CCX/CCD): their ring handoffs stop
# crossing the Infinity Fabric. "split" also keeps guest CPU cores and pipeline/texture workers
# on the other domains. Off by default; the log shows the masks ("Nx2Placement").
# Ryzen 7 3800X, Ocarina in Kokiri Forest: split 28-29 FPS (24 before), wide view 24 (18-19).
EDEN_NX2_PLACEMENT=split
#EDEN_NX2_PLACEMENT=gpu
# Which L3 domain gets the GPU threads (0 = the one with CPU 0; default: the last one).
#EDEN_NX2_PLACEMENT_DOMAIN=0

# Keep every built pipeline for the whole session. By default one unused for 9000 frames is
# destroyed, and a Switch 2 program's pipeline is then translated again on the GPU thread when it
# comes back (the stutter of a first visit, again). 0 = never destroy.
EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_EVICT_FRAMES=0

# Keep textures unused for ~75 s (they were decoded again on coming back). Leave the
# The texture cache collects from 5 GiB on (MaxCriticalMemory caps the driver budget it follows),
# so on a 16 GB card Ocarina evicts the textures of the part of the village behind the camera and
# decodes their ASTC again when the camera turns. Fixed thresholds win over that cap; keep them
# a few GB under the card's budget (16 GB card: ~14 GB).
EDEN_NX2_TC_EXPECTED_MIB=9216
EDEN_NX2_TC_CRITICAL_MIB=11264
EDEN_NX2_TC_OLD_AGE=0

# Build every cached pipeline at boot (longer boot, no stutter for a pipeline seen before).
EDEN_NX2_PRELOAD_ALL_PIPELINES=1

# Cap the pipeline (shader) builder threads (default: logical processors - 1).
#EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_WORKERS=6

# --- Workarounds / Debug ---
# Terrain/indirect drawing fix for Donkey Kong Bananza: enabled by default. Set to 0 only to leave to GPU.
#EDEN_NX2_RESETFIX=0

# Drop reactive-flushing read traps on Switch 2 programs (opt-in; can reduce FPS from 29 to 24 in MKW).
#EDEN_NX2_NO_REACTIVE=1

#EDEN_NX2_MME_JIT=0
#EDEN_NX2_PBFLUSH=0
#EDEN_NX2_SKIP_SAME=0
#EDEN_NX2_INLINE_DEFER=0
#EDEN_NX2_SPLIT_SKIP=1
#EDEN_NX2_AUTO_STUB=1
#EDEN_NX2_KEEP_ASTC=1

# Pipelines that differ only in the types of vertex attributes their shaders never read share
# one pipeline (fewer shader builds in game, fewer pipelines in memory). 0 turns it off.
#EDEN_NX2_VERTEX_KEY_MERGE=0
# Logs what a new pipeline's state differs in from a cached one with the same shaders.
#EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_DIFF=1
